description: Hand a task upwards, where the current holder can act but should not decide alone. The original moves to escalated and is linked to a new task for whoever takes it on. Use chap.handoff.propose to pass work sideways without that link, and chap.control.supersede to replace a task outright. The successor starts with an empty input unless one is supplied, so restate whatever the new assignee needs. A completed, cancelled or superseded task cannot be escalated. The successor takes the mode new_task.mode names, or else the original's, and requires review when the original did, or when it is a trial task under modes/1.0. A paused assignee is refused with -32063, and a mode above the workspace's current ceiling with -32040; after the ceiling is lowered, name a mode within it.

new_task.description: The successor task to open for the escalation target.

assignee.description: Who the escalation goes to. Must be a workspace member who is not paused: a paused assignee is refused with -32063.

input.description: Input payload for the successor. It defaults to an empty object rather than the original's input, so anything the new assignee needs has to be restated here.

kind.description: Task kind for the successor. Defaults to the original's kind.

mode.description: Mode for the successor, defaulting to the original's. A mode above the workspace's current ceiling is refused with -32040, so after the ceiling is lowered a task is escalated by naming a mode within it.

original_task_id.description: The task being escalated. It moves to 'escalated' and is linked to the successor. A completed, cancelled or superseded task cannot be escalated.

name: chap.escalate.raise
title: Escalate task
